extra.message: createInnerHTML() builds an object from decodeURIComponent(document.location.hash), an attacker-controlled source (the URL fragment), and the result is passed directly to React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML at line 54 with no sanitization or encoding. An attacker can craft a URL like '#' and, once a victim opens the link, arbitrary HTML/JavaScript is injected into the DOM and executes in the victim's browser session. The SAMPLE_ATTACK constant on line 6 and the dangerousLinkTo() helper on line 12 demonstrate this exact payload being wired into an in-app link (the 'Exploit me!' button), confirming the sink is reachable via user navigation.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used with markup derived from createInnerHTML(), which returns unsanitized, decoded content from document.location.hash (see lines 26-28). Because the fragment portion of a URL is never sent to a server and is fully attacker-controllable client-side, any HTML/script in the hash is injected verbatim into the DOM, resulting in DOM-based XSS executed in the context of the vulnerable page.
